```{r}
library(terra) 
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap) 
library(kableExtra) 
library(spData) 
library(spDataLarge) 
library(geodata)
```

```{r}
# Read in the data
wc <- st_read('data/wc_regions_clean.shp')
sst_2008 <- rast('data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif')
sst_2009 <- rast('data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif')
sst_2010 <- rast('data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif')
sst_2011 <- rast('data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif')
sst_2012 <- rast('data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif')
depth <- rast('data/depth.tif')
```

```{r}
# Compare SpatRaster geometries
compareGeom(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012, ext = TRUE, res = TRUE, crs = TRUE)

# Stack the rasters
sst <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)
plot(sst) # Check stack worked
```

```{r}
# Check if all dataframe's CRS match
if((st_crs(wc) == crs(sst)) & (crs(sst) == crs(depth))){
  print("It's a match")
} else {
  warning("Coordinate refrence systems do not match")
}
```

```{r}
# Reproject depth to match sst CRS
depth_reprojected <- project(depth, sst)

# Reproject wc to match sst CRS
wc_reprojected <- st_transform(wc, crs(sst))
```

```{r}
# Double check all dataframe's CRS match
if((crs(wc_reprojected) == crs(sst)) & (crs(sst) == crs(depth_reprojected))){
  print("It's a match")
} else {
  warning("Coordinate refrence systems still do not match")
}
```

```{r}
# Take the mean SST from 2008-2012
mean_sst <- app(sst, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Convert average SST from Kelvin to Celsius
mean_sst_c <- mean_sst - 273.15
```

Note: Did not need to manually crop or resample because project() did that

```{r}
# Double check that everything matches
cat("Resolutions match:", all(res(mean_sst_c) == res(depth_reprojected)), "\n")
cat("Origins match:    ", all(round(origin(mean_sst_c), 8) == round(origin(depth_reprojected), 8)), "\n")
cat("Extents match:    ", ext(mean_sst_c) == ext(depth_reprojected), "\n")
cat("CRS match:        ", crs(mean_sst_c) == crs(depth_reprojected), "\n")
cat("Dimensions match:  ", all(dim(mean_sst_c) == dim(depth_reprojected)), "\n")

# Stack rasters
sst_depth <- c(mean_sst_c, depth_reprojected)
plot(sst_depth)
```

```{r}
# Reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for oysters
rcl_depth <- matrix(c(
   -Inf, -70, 0, # Not suitable
   -70, 0, 1, # Suitable
   0, Inf, 0 # Not suitable
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

rcl_sst <- matrix(c(
   -Inf, 11, 0, # Not suitable
   11, 30, 1, # Suitable
   30, Inf, 0 # Not suitable
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

depth_zones <- classify(depth_reprojected, rcl = rcl_depth)
sst_zones <- classify(mean_sst_c, rcl = rcl_sst)

# Stack rasters
suitable_zones <- c(sst_zones, depth_zones)
plot(suitable_zones)
```

```{r}
# Locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions
best_zone <- lapp(suitable_zones, fun = function(s, d) s * d)
names(best_zone) <- "suitable_sst_depth"

plot(best_zone)
```

```{r}
# Convert EEZ regions to raster cells
eez_raster <- rasterize(wc_reprojected, best_zone, field = 'rgn_id')

# Find area of cells
area <- cellSize(best_zone, unit = 'km', mask = TRUE)

# Select suitable depth and sst zone cells within West Coast EEZs
eez_masked <- mask(area, best_zone, maskvalue = 0) # Convert 0 values to NA
plot(eez_masked)

# Summarize cell size variation across the extent
zonal_area <- zonal(eez_masked, eez_raster, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: eez_suitable_area
#| tbl-cap: "Suitable area for marine aquaculture within each West Coast EEZ"

kable(zonal_area,
      col.names = c("EEZ", "Suitable area (km)"),
      digits    = 1
      ) |>
        kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped")
```

```{r}
# Join suitable area onto original vector eez data frame 
map <- left_join(wc_reprojected, zonal_area, by ='rgn_id')
```

```{r}
# Create a map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area
tm_shape(map) +
  tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap') +
  tm_polygons(
      fill = 'area', # Fill polygons based on suitable area
      fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Suitable area (km)',
                              position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center')) 
    ) +
tm_compass(position = c('right', 'top')) +
tm_scalebar(position = c('left', 'bottom')) +
tm_title('Suitable oyster aquaculture area within each EEZ') +
tm_legend(position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center'))
```

The oyster map displays that the central California EEZ has the highest amount of suitable area for oyster aquacultre. The northern California EEZ has the least amount of suitable area.

```{r}
# Create a function of the workflow that can be applied to different species
suitable_aquaculture_eez <- function(species, sst_min, sst_max, depth_min, depth_max) {

  # Stack sst rasters
  sst <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)

  # Reproject depth to match sst CRS
  depth_reprojected <- project(depth, sst)

  # Reproject wc to match sst CRS
  wc_reprojected <- st_transform(wc, crs(sst))

  # Take the mean SST from 2008-2012
  mean_sst <- app(sst, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Convert average SST from Kelvin to Celsius
  mean_sst_c <- mean_sst - 273.15

  # Stack depth and sst rasters
  sst_depth <- c(mean_sst_c, depth_reprojected)

  # Reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for the species
  rcl_depth <- matrix(c(
    -Inf, depth_min, 0, # Not suitable
    depth_min, depth_max, 1, # Suitable
    depth_max, Inf, 0 # Not suitable
  ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

  rcl_sst <- matrix(c(
    -Inf, sst_min, 0, # Not suitable
    sst_min, sst_max, 1, # Suitable
    sst_max, Inf, 0 # Not suitable
  ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

  # Apply zone classification
  depth_zones <- classify(depth_reprojected, rcl = rcl_depth)
  sst_zones <- classify(mean_sst_c, rcl = rcl_sst)

  # Stack classified rasters
  suitable_zones <- c(sst_zones, depth_zones)

  # Calculate locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions
  best_zone <- lapp(suitable_zones, fun = function(s, d) s * d)
  names(best_zone) <- "suitable_sst_depth"

  # Convert EEZ regions to raster cells
  eez_raster <- rasterize(wc_reprojected, best_zone, field = 'rgn_id')

  # Find area of cells
  area <- cellSize(best_zone, unit = 'km', mask = TRUE)

  # Select suitable depth and sst zone cells within West Coast EEZs
  eez_masked <- mask(area, best_zone, maskvalue = 0)

  # Summarize cell size variation across the extent
  zonal_area <- zonal(eez_masked, eez_raster, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

  # Join suitable area onto original vector eez data frame 
  map <- left_join(wc_reprojected, zonal_area, by ='rgn_id')

  # Create a map of EEZ regions colored by amount of suitable area
  aquaculture_map <- tm_shape(map) +
                      tm_basemap('OpenStreetMap') +
                      tm_polygons(
                          fill = 'area', # Fill polygons based on suitable area
                          fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'Suitable area (km)',
                                                  position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center')) 
                        ) +
                    tm_compass(position = c('right', 'top')) +
                    tm_scalebar(position = c('left', 'bottom')) +
                    tm_title(paste('Suitable', species, 'aquaculture area within each EEZ')) +
                    tm_legend(position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center'))

  return(aquaculture_map)
}
```
```{r}
suitable_aquaculture_eez(species = 'red abalone', sst_min = 10, sst_max = 18, depth_min = 6, depth_max = 40)
```

The red abalone map displays that the Washington EEZ has the highest amount of suitable aquaculture area. The northern California EEZ has the least amount of suitable area.
